thread:
incident-bot: PAGED: suspicious S3 write + auth traffic spike detected for redwood-prod-logs bucket. priority=P1. tagging oncall.
maya: acked. i'm oncall, joining now. what's the customer impact?
oncall-sre: ack. i see write spikes from an IP range 45.33.12.0/24 to s3://redwood-prod-logs/edge/2026-03-16/ -- multiple small gz parts. suspicious user agent 'logshipper/1.2'.
eli: adding context: we correlate with auth-proxy metrics, a subset of requests had 200s after repeated 403s. could be stolen svc token or misconfigured forwarder.
sarah: copying security-eng and legal. @security-eng can you confirm if any secrets appear in the uploaded files before we scrub?
security-eng: pulling a sample now. attaching hash refs and filenames. found truncated lines that look like header dumps. sample path: s3://redwood-prod-logs/edge/2026-03-16/part-0007.gz
opsbot: automated scan: file part-0007.gz contains strings matching "API-Key: sk_live_" (redacted) and "session_token=" -- flagged for immediate containment.
maya: :grimacing: ok, treat as data exposure. isolating bucket access now. @oncall-sre please run quick policy lock.
oncall-sre: executed: set-bucket-policy --bucket redwood-prod-logs --block-public true; removed external write role redwood-logshipper-forwarder-extern -- command output ok.
eli: can we avoid deleting objects until security confirms whether customer PII is present? we should snapshot and export for forensics.
security-eng: agreed. made read-only snapshot and copied suspect objects to infra-forensics (encrypted). started integrity hash and grep for tokens. preliminary: 6 objects contain partial API key fragments, none with full 40-char key but there are 16 char prefixes.
legal: flagging legal hold. please preserve originals. we may need to notify customers depending on token reconstruction risk.
maya: action list so far: 1) lock bucket (done) 2) snapshot forensics (done) 3) rotate affected svc tokens and any exposed keys (plan needed) 4) scope customer impact 5) comms plan w/legal.
security-eng: ETA on full grep: ~15m. recommend immediate rotation of service account used by logshipper-forwarder-idp (svc-logs-forwarder). initiating rotation now and will push new creds to vault.
oncall-sre: starting rotation cmd: svcctl rotate-key --svc svc-logs-forwarder --reason "suspected leak" --notify vault
opsbot: rotation job queued, deployment-scale=2. Expect rolling update to forwarders in 2-3 mins.
eli: quick check: any downstream consumers of that service account? list: log-indexer, metrics-aggregator, retention-worker. will coordinate rapid reconfigure.
maya: customer impact assessment: no direct user traffic degradation observed. potential risk: if adversary reconstructs full keys from fragments they could call internal endpoints. until we know, treat as high-risk.
security-eng: grep done. found 4 lines with prefix sk_live_ab12cd34... truncated at 16 chars. can't reconstruct full key reliably but cannot rule out exfil from other sources. recommending global rotate for any keys with that prefix pattern and revoke stale tokens created in last 72h.
sarah: legal says file a sec incident report and prepare a customer notification draft if we see confirmed token misuse. for now classify as 'suspected exposure'.
maya: who will take lead on notifications and timeline? @legal to draft, @ops for customer comms.
legal: drafting now. need timeline and scope from security. target initial stash to exec in 60m, customer notice TBD based on misuse evidence.
eli: I'll run a quick internal search across logging pipelines to see if the same forwarder wrote elsewhere. give me 10m.
oncall-sre: also enabling WAF rules for suspicious UA 'logshipper/1.2' on edge for 24h. rule applied.
opsbot: added ephemeral denylist for IP range 45.33.12.0/24 at edge-proxy.
security-eng: confirmed additional writes to a staging bucket redwood-staging-logs from same IPs. staging objects contain full api-key strings in 2 files. opening separate evidence folder.
maya: urgent: rotate any customer-facing API keys that match prefixes we found. ops, can we automate rotate + retry for customers with high-risk keys?
opsbot: running batch rotate for keys with prefix patterns sk_live_ab12* in customer-keystore. estimated 45 keys. starting now.
eli: note: backup plan for app outages: if rotation breaks downstream integrations we'll fallback to scoped temp tokens and extend TTLs for infra-critical paths while we update configs.
security-eng: I will prepare a post-incident forensics note with hashes, object list, and recommended rotation lists. expect list in ~90m.
maya: status check in 30m at #incident-bridge. assign follow-ups: security-eng forensic lead, eli infra rebuilds, oncall-sre policy+waf, legal+maya comms.
opsbot: incident-bot: incident updated to mitigation stage. incident-id=INC-2026-0316-42. paging paging@sec-team for 30m follow-up.
maya: thanks team. keep updates concise in this thread. :thumbsup:
